newsitem.title: USA: Dunavant sees 97/98 world cotton output 87.3 mln.
newsitem.headline: Dunavant sees 97/98 world cotton output 87.3 mln.

text.p: Cotton merchant Willian B. Dunavant Jr. projected 1997/98 world cotton output at 87.3 million 480-lb bales compared with an estimated 86.3 million bales this crop season.
He based his estimate 76.50 cents per pound December cotton futures on the New York Cotton Exchange and 83.7 million planted cotton acres. This compares 84.1 million acres planted in 1996/97.
World cotton consumption in 1997/98 was projected at 86.8 million bales and world carryover at 36.5 million bales. Dunavant estimated world carryover will reach 36.0 million bales in 1996/97.
China, he said, will produce 18.35 million bales and will consume no more than 20 million bales in 1997/98.
"Remember, when you deal with China it always projections," Dunavant said. "Just as in the U.S.,the price of competing crops is going to be the major factor, but not as major as it is in the U.S."
